evals.prompt:
Hey, I need to add a new project to my portfolio. Here's the raw info:

Product: InvenTrack - a B2B inventory management platform for mid-market retail chains
Problem: Store managers were spending 2+ hours daily on manual stock reconciliation across 3 different screens. The existing inventory view was basically a giant table with no filtering or alerts.
My role: Solo designer, worked with 4 engineers and 1 PM
What I did: Ran 6 interviews with store managers, did a contextual inquiry at 2 retail locations. Discovered the core issue was that managers needed predictive alerts, not just current stock levels. Designed a unified inventory dashboard with smart alerts, threshold-based reordering, and a mobile-responsive view for in-store use.
Shipped in 8 weeks. Live since Oct 2024.
Results: Stock-out incidents dropped 45%, managers reported saving 90+ min/day, adopted by 340+ stores within 2 months.

Can you create the case study page for my Next.js portfolio?
evals.expected_output: A complete Next.js case study page component with: impact-first headline (not 'Redesigning InvenTrack'), hero section with 3 metric callouts, full narrative following the 8-section structure, ownership language throughout, no explicit seniority claims, production/live emphasis, and proper TypeScript/responsive code.

evals.prompt:
I want to add my biggest project. Here's everything:

Product: Nexus Platform - enterprise workflow automation for compliance teams at financial institutions
Timeline: 5 months, 2023-2024
Team: I was lead designer with 1 junior designer reporting to me, 8 engineers, 2 PMs, worked closely with compliance SMEs
Problem: Compliance teams were using a patchwork of spreadsheets and email chains to manage audit workflows. Average audit prep took 3 weeks. Errors in documentation were causing regulatory findings. The existing tool had been built by engineers with no design input.
Research: 12 user interviews, shadowed 3 audit cycles, analyzed 6 months of support tickets, ran a design sprint with stakeholders
Solution: End-to-end audit workflow management system with automated document collection, real-time collaboration, approval chains, and an audit trail dashboard. I also established the design system for the platform.
Design decisions: Chose a progressive disclosure pattern for complex forms (compliance forms can have 200+ fields). Designed an 'audit confidence score' visualization that gave teams real-time readiness status. Pushed back on a PM request to add a chatbot - research showed users wanted structured workflows, not conversational UI.
Results: Audit prep time reduced from 3 weeks to 4 days. Zero regulatory findings in first 2 audits post-launch. Adopted by 15 financial institutions. Led to $2M ARR expansion. NPS went from 28 to 67.
Reflection: This project taught me how to design for highly regulated industries. The biggest lesson was that in compliance, 'delightful' means 'trustworthy and predictable,' not 'clever and novel.'
evals.expected_output: The most comprehensive case study - should showcase leadership (mentored junior designer), strategic pushback (chatbot decision), domain expertise (regulated industry), and business impact ($2M ARR). The headline should be powerful. The design decisions section should be particularly detailed. Reflection should include the user's own insight about 'delightful means trustworthy.'
